content:
"Just a sec."


I asked a straightforward question in a grievance meeting. There was a pause while they typed. Then out came an answer so smooth...

Beautifully structured. Perfectly calm. About as personal as a press release. 

That kind of polish doesn't happen by accident when it's your own grievance.

So the The HR Vault's grievance procedures have a new line or two. Optional lines.

AI tools are not permitted during a grievance or appeal meeting. If you're asked a question, you answer it yourself. No typing it into a chatbot mid meeting and reading back whatever comes out. The one exception is an AI tool agreed in advance as a reasonable adjustment, arranged with the manager hearing it before the meeting starts.

While I was in there I also capped the written grievance at two pages, with an executive summary if the grievance does need to be longer. I don't need the full written history across 70 pages.

That's what the meeting is for 😅

content:
For a while, I've been trying to work out the best way for me to talk about HR and the Employment Rights Act in written form. 


It didn't feel right to include it on my business websites, because it's not really part of my business. 

So I have done a thing. And bought a domain which is literally just my name. 

It feels like a thing that's very unlike me. 

But it means I can share my actual thoughts with the world! 

And I hope it might lead to more opinion and comments in the press about HR and the absolute  💩  we have to put up with people saying about us. 

My first article is titled "The Real Problem with HR Isn't HR" - and it serves as a reminder to some that HR could be the difference between a criminal charge and a massive fine. 

Read it here: https://lnkd.in/gJMMBmWk

content:
Prevention of (sexual) harassment guidance is changing again next month. 


"Reasonable steps" to prevent it is now "all reasonable steps". 

I don't actually see the difference, but what do I know. 

And employers have to take steps to prevent third-parties from harassing employees. Note: this is not just sexual harassment, it is all forms of harassment. 

I once told a room full of pub managers about this and they all literally laughed at me. Anyway... 

Again, all of my prevention of sexual harassment risk assessments already featured third-parties. Because my risk assessments were based on the existing ECHR guidance. 

Anyway, if you're as confused about all of this as I am, my latest article on this topic from The HR Vault can be found here: https://lnkd.in/gPYd9ZJb 

You can download updated harassment policies and risk assessments from the Vault now too!

🫠 Here’s the dilemma from last night:


I am dealing with a tricky employee who is using AI to handle their grievance. 

I just want to get them to come to the hearing so that I can help. 

I want to know if they have sent a further email with some more quotes from made up legislation. 

But it’s 8pm.

And I know that if I read it now, it’ll wind me up and I won’t be able to sleep. 

Buuuuuut… I’m not going to be able to sleep thinking about the possibilities of the reply, which I have no doubt will be long, entitled (full of unreasonable non-Acas compliant demands) and make little-to-no sense. 

Dilemma. 

Yes. I am tired today 🥱
